$comment: THE BLIND CORPUS. Frozen BEFORE the scorer that answers it was written, and committed on its own
so the order is checkable in git rather than asserted here.
IT RECORDS NO EXPECTED ANSWER, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A corpus carrying the outcome its author
wanted is a restatement of the scorer, not a test of it: tuning until the expectations go green
proves the tuning terminated. Every brief therefore carries `expected: null`. The picks are judged
GOOD / DEFENSIBLE / WRONG by a reviewer who did not write the scorer, who is not told what any
outcome should be, and who is told that DECLINING is one of the outcomes available to it.
`ambiguous: true` marks the briefs whose medium genuinely fits both engines. There is no unique
right answer there and demanding one would be demanding luck; DEFENSIBLE is a pass.
`availability` names the capability context each brief is asked in, because three of these are
about the HARD filter rather than about matching: a perfect match that did not clear review, a
perfect match on a runtime this chain does not carry, and a medium no engine in the wave draws.
